fields.front: Norwegian (Bokmål) word or phrase; nouns with article in parentheses, e.g. (en) mann, (en/ei) kvinne; verbs with å
fields.inflections: inflected forms, e.g. å gå, gikk gått
fields.type: one of noun, verb, adjective, adverb, phrase, idiom
fields.subtype: optional, e.g. infinitive, simple past, past participle, proper, time

conventions: Leave front_add, back_add, front_hint, back_hint, scratch empty unless the user asks.
Voice 'no' (Google Norwegian) reading front as-is, parenthesized articles included; the user approved how it sounds.

fields.Text: (part of speech) definition. Example sentence with the word as {{c1::word}}. The cloze holds the base (dictionary) form; inflection endings go outside it, e.g. {{c1::enervate}}d. No IPA by default (the audio covers pronunciation); add it only when the pronunciation is genuinely not obvious from the spelling, e.g. {{c1::chimerical /kaɪˈmer.ɪ.kəl/}}

conventions: Audio speaks only the cloze word: use add_audio with cloze_only=true (IPA and hints are dropped).
For new notes via add_notes, set audio.text to the plain base-form cloze word without transcription or endings (e.g. 'enervate', not 'enervated').

Google en-US (and en-CA) mispronounces some rare words, e.g. chimerical; en-GB got it right. If the user reports a wrong pronunciation, they clear Back Extra in Anki and you re-voice that one note with en-GB; if en-GB is wrong too, try macos:Samantha (used for kvetch).
The user may supply a definition and example; keep their example unless asked to improve it, and pick an example that actually shows the meaning.
Also tag 'duolingo' if the sentence comes from Duolingo.
Never put the sound tag in Front too: the templates already play Audio with the Latin side.
Set audio.text to the plain Latin text with macrons (e.g. 'cīvitātēs'), even when Front has none: the voice takes vowel length and stress from them. Never generate speech from HTML.
Voice is a self-trained Classical Latin Piper voice; Google's 'la' is not Latin. Fallback: 'espeak:la'.

fields.Front: Spanish word or sentence as the user encountered it, correct spelling, accents and punctuation; nouns with article. Only the main answer, no HTML. A short alternative (gender ending, synonym) may follow in brackets, e.g. 'cansado (cansada)'; leave long alternatives out.
fields.Back: natural English translation; several natural ones separated by ' / '. A short note may follow in brackets (under ~40 chars), e.g. '(informal)', '(From Duolingo)'; leave long notes out.
fields.Audio: filled by the audio step ([sound:...]); never write it by hand

conventions: Plain two-way type (user, 2026-10-04): card 1 Spanish->English, card 2 English->Spanish. It replaced the custom 'Spanish MC + Typing' type, which broke on AnkiDroid. No choices/decoys, no <span class="alt"> markup.
This deck is for everything the user adds by hand, unrelated to Pimsleur.

Example sentences are their own notes: Front = Spanish sentence, Back = English translation, extra tag 'example', with their own audio. Only when the user asks for examples; never add them unprompted.
Audio speaks only the Spanish Front text, without the bracketed alternative (set audio.text to the main answer).
If the user says where the word came from, put it in brackets at the end of Back, e.g. '(From Duolingo)'.

fields.Word: Spanish word, nouns with article (la cumbre); expressions as-is
fields.WordType: one of N, V, Adj, Adv, Expr, Prep, Pron, Conj, Num
fields.Gender: m, f or m/f for nouns; empty otherwise

conventions: Leave Word_suffix, Word_hint, Meaning_suffix, Meaning_hint empty.
Tag Spanish::Duolingo::<nn>_<Topic> if the user names a matching topic.
